title: Model batch
description: An atomic batch of element creates, updates and deletes, database schema operations, materialize operations, binding operations, process operations, tag operations, the names-to-ids refactor, the text-to-trees conversion, the fold into a stereotype, the reference-type refactors and the verb operations, from the editor, a refactoring or an AI proposal.

id.description: The element: an id, a qualified name (@kind:path) or a placeholder ($name). A create's id must be an id; an update's or delete's must not be a placeholder; an upsert's must be a qualified name. For sync-enum and sync-codes, the lifecycle process; for fold-into-stereotype, the stereotype whose members the tables adopt; for rename-code, retire-code and rename-reference-type, the reference type; for merge-reference-types, the reference type merged away.

as.description: Create, update and upsert: a placeholder that names the operation's element for the whole batch.

resolution.description: What a delete does with references to the element: refuse (the default) while anything references it, remove-references to clear optional references, or delete-dependents to also remove or delete what cannot exist without it (delete only).

element.description: The element document. Its references may be qualified names or placeholders, and an object whose schema requires an id may carry as; the engine mints every missing id below the root.

value.description: The translated text, a sidecar reference, or null to remove the translation.

database.description: The database: an id, a qualified name or a placeholder (materialize-tables, materialize-entities, materialize-attributes, materialize-columns, map-by-name, resync-binding).

entities.description: The entities, each an id, a qualified name or a placeholder, that get a designed table and a binding (materialize-tables), or that get an attribute per column of the source of their binding to the database (materialize-attributes), or a column of their table per attribute their binding leaves unmapped (materialize-columns), or whose binding to the database is mapped by name (map-by-name) or brought into step with its table (resync-binding).

tables.description: The designed or imported tables and the views, each an id, a qualified name or a placeholder, that get an entity and a binding (materialize-entities); the designed or imported tables whose own members the stereotype's replace (fold-into-stereotype).

package.description: The package the new entities go to (materialize-entities); the domain whose tag vocabulary it is (retag, tags-to-property; absent for the global one). An id, a qualified name or a placeholder.

columns.description: The columns of the source, as keys or physical names, that get an attribute mapped to them (materialize-attributes, one entity only; absent means every column nothing in the binding names), or that a re-sync brings into step, updating only their provenance entries (resync-binding, one entity only; absent means every column of the source).

attributes.description: The binding field references (attribute ids, attributeId.memberId for a value object member, to-one end ids) that get a column of the entity's table mapped to them (materialize-columns, one entity only); absent means every attribute the binding leaves unmapped. An item that starts with @ or $ names one attribute or end; the composite attributeId.memberId stays ids.

elementIds.description: The elements names-to-ids, tags-to-property, text-to-trees and use-subjects act on, each an id, a qualified name or a placeholder; absent means every element they apply to (names-to-ids: every document with x-ref sites; tags-to-property: every holder the vocabulary governs, and the moved tags' declarations leave the vocabulary; text-to-trees: every document that holds an expression as text; use-subjects: every process in the one-subject form, which it rewrites as subjects with one entry).

tags.description: The tag keys to remove, or the one to rename (retag).

prefix.description: The prefix of the tags that move into the property name (tags-to-property): each tag that starts with it and leaves a non-empty suffix.

expectedHashes.description: Materialize, map-by-name, resync-binding, retag, tags-to-property, names-to-ids, fold-into-stereotype, the reference-type refactors, rename-verb and remove-verb: the hash the caller read of each element it expects the operation to change or delete (the preview's updates and deletes). Given, an element that changed since, or that the operation changes but the map does not name, is a conflict and nothing is written, so an undo built from what the caller read never puts back a stale version. A key may be a qualified name, never a placeholder.

schema.description: The database schema: an id, a qualified name or a placeholder (rename-schema, remove-schema, set-default-schema; optional for add-schema; for materialize-tables, the schema the tables go to, else each projected table's own; for fold-into-stereotype, the schema whose designed and imported tables are folded: those that state it, or state none when it is the default).

name.description: The schema name (add-schema, rename-schema); the new key of the one tag (retag; absent removes the tags); the custom property the tags move to (tags-to-property); the reference type's new name (rename-reference-type).

code.description: The code a refactor acts on, as the code's canonical text (an integer in decimal digits, a uuid in lowercase): the code to rename (rename-code) or to retire (retire-code).

verb.description: The key of the project's own verb a verb operation acts on (rename-verb, remove-verb). A built-in verb's key, or a key no own verb has, refuses the operation (MQ1002).

to.description: The code's new text (rename-code), or the live code whose row takes over the retired code's uses (retire-code); the verb's new key (rename-verb): another own verb's or a built-in verb's key merges the two, the uses moving to it and the definition going with its translations.

codes.description: merge-reference-types: codes of the merged-away type mapped to live codes of the target, for codes the target does not hold itself; every other code moves into the target as a row.

entity.description: The subject whose binding the operation acts on: an id, a qualified name or a placeholder. sync-enum: the subject whose bound enum is synced; absent means the lifecycle's one enum binding, in either subject form. sync-codes: the subject whose attribute holds the state; on a lifecycle in the one-subject form it must be that subject, on one that lists subjects an entity not listed gets an entry, and a lifecycle with no subject gets subjects with one entry. sync-codes reads the model as it was before the batch, so its entity must name an existing entity (an id or a qualified name, not a placeholder).

stereotype.description: sync-enum and sync-codes, in place of entity: the key of the stereotype whose subjects entry the operation acts on. sync-enum syncs the enum that entry binds; sync-codes binds one of the stereotype's own attributes in that entry, which the lifecycle must already list.

attribute.description: sync-codes: the attribute of entity (own, inherited or from a stereotype), or of stereotype (its own), that holds the state, single-valued and typed by an enum, a reference type or a plain status (string, text, int16, int32 or int64, directly or through a scalar type). The operation binds it in the form the file has. It must name an existing attribute (an id or a qualified name, not a placeholder): sync-codes reads the model as it was before the batch.

stateCodes.description: sync-codes: codes keyed by state id (or a state's qualified name), each a string or an integer; a listed state takes its code, replacing one it has. Every other state that needs a code keeps the one it has, else takes the one code of the attribute's type equal to its name (case, _ and - ignored), else the one row whose label equals its display name or name; an ambiguous match takes none. The operation creates no rows.

target.description: The schema that the tables, views, sequences, convention entries and mappings of the removed schema move to (remove-schema); the process the entity follows, or absent to clear the lifecycle (set-lifecycle); the child state that becomes the initial one (set-initial); the reference type merged into (merge-reference-types). An id, a qualified name or a placeholder.

default.description: The schema that becomes the default when the removed schema is the default (remove-schema): an id, a qualified name or a placeholder.

redefine.description: fold-into-stereotype: where an own member differs from the stereotype's in a facet a redefinition may state, write a redefines entry with the table's value instead of refusing the table.

excludeMissing.description: fold-into-stereotype: exclude each member of the stereotype a table lacks instead of refusing the table, so the fold adds nothing to the database.

keepNames.description: resync-binding: keep every attribute's name, even one that followed its column's name; the provenance entry still takes the column's new name.

triggerPoints.description: refresh-scenario: also write each step's expect.triggerPoints, the trigger points that ran in order (skipped ones left out); without it they are rewritten only where a step already expects them.

placeholder.description: A name a batch declares with as and uses anywhere in the batch.

qualifiedName.description: An element or sub-element by kind and stored name: @kind:path, its segments separated by dots, a segment with a dot, quote or white space written in double quotes.

idOrName.description: An id, a qualified name or a placeholder.
